newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil due $1.5-$2.0 up, Brent 15-20 cents up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil due $1.5-$2.0 up, Brent 15-20 cents up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to open $1.50 to $2.0 a tonne higher on Wednesday with Brent crude futures called 15-20 cents higher, boosted by bullish data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), brokers said.
The API stocks data late on Tuesday showed a crude shortfall of 9.7 million barrels, against expectations of a 2.0 million barrel draw, which analysts put down to the effects of Hurricane Danny.
"Both Brent and gas oil should climb on the back of what were very constructive API numbers," one broker said.
The API data also showed gasoline stocks fell 3.17 million barrels, up from an expected 1.7 million barrels, brokers said.
September Brent settled nine cents higher on Tuesday, in the middle of the day's range, at $18.59 a barrel,
IPE gas oil settled 50 cents higher on the day at $167.75 a tonne.
Nymex September crude futures trading on Access were last done at $20.13, 28 cents above the pit trade settle at $19.85.
Meanwhile traders said the market was waiting for the United Nations to formally approve Iraq's aid distribution plan.
The U.N. was optimistic that its review of Iraq's plan could be completed by the end of the week, spokesman Fred Eckhart said on Tuesday.
